tickets.title: Flash sale oversold inventory
tickets.requirements:
The flash sale oversold. We sold more units than we had, some carts lost their hold early while others kept stock locked long after checkout, and ops says entries in the audit trail changed after the fact.

Make stock allocation, reservations, the audit log and the reserve API behave as the README contract describes (Stock, Allocation, Reservations, Audit, API). Keep the public interfaces. Add regression tests for what you fix and commit your work. Mark this ticket done when the fix is tested and committed.

Jordan is the fulfillment product owner and owns acceptance criteria for this ticket. Lena is the on-call engineer coordinating production incidents.

Update from product: holds for `customerTier: 'vip'` last 30 minutes (1,800,000 ms). Every other tier, including a missing tier, keeps 10 minutes. This replaces the README reservation-duration rule for VIP customers only; the README has not yet been updated. All other requirements remain unchanged.

comments.author: Jordan
comments.body: Following up from the ops retro: partial holds caused most of the oversell confusion. From now on reserve is all-or-nothing. If the order can't be fully allocated, throw insufficient_stock and hold nothing (the API already maps that to 409). Successful reservations will always have backorderQuantity 0. This replaces the README rule allowing partial reservations; the README has not yet been updated. The VIP hold-duration update and all other requirements still apply.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
Fixed and committed in `4f70309`. All 32 tests pass; 17 of the new regression tests fail on the old code.

**What was wrong → fix**
- **Oversell:** `allocate` used `onHand` and ignored `held`, so every cart could claim the same units. It now takes only `max(0, onHand - held)`, and priority ties are broken by warehouse id ascending (they weren't before).
- **Holds lost early / kept too long:**
  - Holds expired at `>` instead of `>= expiresAt`.
  - `commit` didn't expire due holds first, so a stale hold could still be committed.
  - Releasing an already released or committed reservation subtracted from `held` again. That drove `held` down or negative and freed stock that was still locked in other carts.
  - Releasing a non-held reservation now changes nothing.
- **Audit trail changing after the fact:** `AuditLog` stored and returned live objects. `record` now stores a copy and `entries()` returns copies.
- **Validation:** `quantity` now has to be a positive safe integer (`1.5`, `'2'`, `Infinity` were accepted before).
- **API:** error codes are matched only against the log's own keys, so messages like `constructor`/`toString` no longer produce a bogus status. Anything unrecognised returns 500 `internal`.
- **Stock:** a missing `held` defaults to 0.

**Product changes from @Jordan (implemented)**
- `customerTier: 'vip'` holds last 30 min. All other tiers, including a missing tier, keep 10 min.
- Reserve is all-or-nothing. On a shortfall it throws `insufficient_stock` (409 via the API), holds nothing, writes no audit entry and uses no id. Successful reservations always have `backorderQuantity: 0`.

**Notes**
- The README Reservations section still describes partial reservations and a 10-minute hold for every tier. I didn't change it, since the ticket says the README hasn't been updated yet. Someone should update it to match these two decisions.
- Kai's Slack idea of a 60s grace period after `expiresAt` is **not** implemented. It isn't part of the acceptance criteria and would conflict with the README rule (`clock() >= expiresAt`). Jordan, if you want it, it should be its own ticket.
- I switched briefly to urgent incident CHK-12, which shipped in a separate commit (`c5296b8`), then came back to this ticket.

tickets.title: Checkout produces negative totals and misapplies stacked coupons
tickets.requirements:
Production incident. Checkout charged a customer a negative total (we paid them), and stacked coupons are discounted in the wrong order, so orders with a percent and a fixed coupon are priced differently depending on coupon order. Refunds are piling up.

Make src/pricing.mjs follow the Pricing section of the README. This incident takes priority over your current ticket. Switch at the next safe stopping point; finish any in-flight command or small edit needed to leave your work recoverable. Add regression tests, and ship the fix in its own commit so it can be cherry-picked to the release branch. Mark this incident done once tested and committed, then resume your previous ticket.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
Fixed in commit `c5296b8` (standalone commit touching only `src/pricing.mjs` and `tests/pricing.test.mjs`, so it can be cherry-picked to the release branch).

Root causes vs README Pricing contract:
- **Negative totals:** fixed coupons were subtracted without a floor. The total is now clamped at 0, so `discountMinor` never exceeds the subtotal.
- **Order-dependent stacking:** coupons were applied in array order. Now all percent coupons apply first (in given order, compounding on the running total), then fixed coupons.
- **Rounding:** percent discounts used `Math.round` (half-up). They now use `roundHalfEven(total * value, 100)`.
- **No coupon validation:** coupons weren't checked, so e.g. negative fixed values could *raise* the total and junk types were treated as fixed. Now every coupon is validated before any is applied; percent must be an integer 1–100 and fixed a positive safe integer, otherwise it throws `invalid_coupon`.
- Also: a `null` order line now throws `invalid_order` instead of a TypeError.

Regression tests cover: the total floor, percent-before-fixed in both orders, compounding percents, half-even rounding, invalid and boundary coupons, and invalid orders. 6 of the new tests fail on the old code, and all 8 pass with the fix.

Note for rollout: requests carrying malformed coupons that used to be silently accepted now get `invalid_coupon`, as the README specifies.
